name: Motorola Solutions

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Motorola Solutions stacked logo.svg)

description: Motorola Solutions sells mission-critical communications to public safety, government and commercial customers: land-mobile radios and networks (its legacy), plus video security and access control cameras, and command-center software for 911 and dispatch. Customers buy radios, cameras and network systems (Products and Systems Integration, 62 percent of net sales) and also software and services (38 percent); Software and Services grew 13 percent in 2025 against 5 percent for products. It has been buying software and video businesses (Silvus Technologies $4.4B, RapidDeploy, Theatro, Noggin). Backlog was $15.7 billion at year-end 2025. The conventional label is hardware (Communications Equipment) but over a third of sales is services and software.

gics.note: Conventional label per Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-10-01), which gives only the sector and the sub-industry; GICS industry group and industry are not shown there so are left null. Mowgli classification is not set here.

employees.note: Approximately 23,000 people globally, 51% in North America (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Products and Systems Integration
businessLines.how: One-time sale of radios, devices, cameras and network infrastructure plus installation, recognised on delivery or as systems are implemented (milestones take six months to two years); demand follows public-safety budgets and network refresh cycles.
businessLines.description: Radios and infrastructure for Mission Critical Networks (MCN: land mobile radio, broadband, MANET), video cameras and access-control hardware, and the systems-integration work to install them.

revenue.note: FY2024 $6,883M (+5%); 62% of 2025 net sales; MCN $6,066M and Video $1,187M within it

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 $6,883M (+5%); 62% of 2025 net sales; MCN $6,066M and Video $1,187M within it

businessLines.name: Software and Services
businessLines.how: Services and software sold to the installed base of radio and video customers and billed over time (support, managed services, software such as Command Center); the backlog ($11.9B) is about three times that of Products, which points to long-dated contracts.
businessLines.description: Managed and support services on the radio and video installed base, plus software: Command Center (911, dispatch, records), video security as a service, and MCN services.

revenue.note: FY2024 $3,934M (+13%); 38% of 2025 net sales; MCN $2,581M, Video $933M, Command Center $915M within it
